newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta index ends down in cautious trading.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta index ends down in cautious trading.

text.p: Jakarta shares ended down in cautious trading on Monday amid a lack of fresh domestic factors, brokers said.
The Jakarta composite index fell 1.98 points, or 0.31 percent, to close at 635.17 points. Decliners led advancers by 120 to 63 with 78 issues unchanged.
Total turn-over was some 524 billion rupiah against 388 billion rupiah on Friday, brokers said.
"Overall, the market tone remained cautious. There was some active buying of shares belonging to the Lippo Group, but the buying did not have much impact on the index," one broker said.
Brokers said the tone on many big-capitalised stocks was likely to remain generally soft due to cautious sentiment ahead of the general elections in late May.
"Sentiment is likely to stay soft on worries that fresh riots may erupt again ahead of the general election," one said.
Brokers said most shares beloging to the Lippo Group conglomerate rose in active trading, but reasons were not clear.

Lippo Life rose 375 rupiah to 2,750 rupiah, Lippo Securities was up 125 rupiah to 1,350 rupiah while Multipolar and Lippo Bank each gained 50 rupiah to end at 1,425 rupiah and 2,400 rupiah respectively.
One analyst said brokerage firm Lippo Securities remained attractive despite the rise due to expected strong earnings growth this year.
Lippo Securities said in early March it expected to post a net profit of 87 billion rupiah in 1997 against 40.4 billion rupiah in 1996.
Second-liner property firms including Bhuwanatala, Suryamas Dutamakmur, and Pudjiadi and Duta Pertiwi were among active counters for speculative reasons, brokers said.
